backward_compat_traps.rule: CANopen is the application layer ABOVE CAN; it reuses the CAN frame, arbitration, bit stuffing, and error frame unchanged.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating CANopen as a redefinition of the CAN data link layer is wrong — a raw CAN controller with no object dictionary / PDO / SDO / NMT is NOT CANopen.

backward_compat_traps.rule: PDOs are exchanged only in the Operational state.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Expecting PDO traffic in Pre-operational or Stopped is wrong.

backward_compat_traps.rule: A device uses heartbeat OR node guarding, not both.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Enabling both error-control mechanisms at once is non-conformant.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The COB-ID maps to the CAN identifier; the predefined connection set allocates defaults from the Node-ID.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming the COB-ID is independent of the CAN identifier is wrong.

fields.version_naming_history_note: CANopen is standardized by CAN in Automation (CiA) as CiA 301, the application layer and communication profile, registered as the European standard EN 50325-4. The version 4 series (v4.0 / v4.1 / v4.2.0) defines the object dictionary, the PDO/SDO/NMT/SYNC/TIME/EMCY/heartbeat communication objects, the COB-ID predefined connection set, and the NMT boot-up state machine. Companion specs (CiA 305 LSS, CiA 306 EDS, CiA 401 / 402 device profiles) build on CiA 301.
